region: Antigua, Lake Atitlán, the western highlands and the Petén jungle
title: Guatemala — Volcanoes and the Lost Cities of the Maya
subtitle: Fuego's night glow, Tz'utujil lakeside villages, K'iche' markets and Tikal's towers in one 13-day arc
summary: A 13-day route from colonial Antigua over volcano ridges and Maya lake and highland towns to the temples of Tikal and Yaxhá, using hired drivers and one domestic flight instead of self-drive.
introduction: The trip opens in Antigua, where baroque ruins sit under three volcanoes, and climbs to a cold overnight camp to watch Fuego throw glowing rock into the dark, if the post-eruption ascent ban has been lifted. It then drops to Lake Atitlán, where Tz'utujil cooperatives dye cotton with plants, crosses to Chichicastenango on a Thursday market day, and climbs to Xela for a dawn hike over the Santiaguito lava dome. A short flight to the Petén ends with sunrise at Tikal, a night under canvas near the temples and sunset at Yaxhá.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman is empty roads, sand and wadis in your own vehicle. Guatemala is the opposite: vertical, cold, forested and densely populated, with Maya communities, active volcanoes and no self-drive because of crime and carjacking risk.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Standard circuits stay in Antigua, Panajachel and a Tikal day trip. This route spends nights at a volcano camp, in a Tz'utujil lakeside village and inside Tikal, and goes to Xela's Santa María and Zunil instead of repeating the market-and-lake loop.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: Only Guatemala combines an active Strombolian volcano in view all night, living Maya markets and rituals, and the large jungle cities of the Classic Maya within 13 days and one domestic flight.

duration.note: Day 1 outbound flight with arrival the same day assumed; day 13 return flight. Includes one domestic flight each way to the Petén.

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: Dry season, cool highland nights, Lent Sundays with procession alfombras in Antigua, and before the March start of Petén field-burning haze and the extreme crowds and prices of Holy Week (21–28 March 2027).

februarySuitability.summary: Dry in both the highlands and the Petén, clear volcano views at night, cooler lowland heat and the first Sundays of Lent; highland nights near freezing.

marchSuitability.summary: Still dry, but hotter in the Petén (about 33 °C), more field burning, and demand and prices rise towards Semana Santa from 21 March; early March before Holy Week is workable.

climate.regionNote: Antigua (1,500 m) normals from Wikipedia; Flores/Mundo Maya airport 1991–2020 normals; summit and Xela nights are estimates from altitude (Xela 2,330 m, Acatenango camp about 3,500 m).

february.rainfall: 3 mm in Antigua; about 35 mm in the Petén
february.humidity: Low in the highlands; humid in the Petén
february.notes: Day highs range from Antigua 23 °C to Flores 31 °C; nights from about 0 °C at altitude to 18 °C in the lowlands (altitude nights estimated).

march.rainfall: 4 mm in Antigua; about 36 mm in the Petén
march.humidity: Low in the highlands; humid in the Petén
march.notes: Petén reaches 33 °C on average; haze from burning peaks in March–April (established pattern, no 2027 forecast).

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: No snow, but frost at 3,500 m and above. Acatenango camp nights can drop below 0 °C; clear skies in the dry season. Ascent status of Acatenango and Fuego is restricted after the August 2026 eruption and must be re-checked.
climate.seaConditions: Not relevant: no coast on the route. Lake Atitlán's Xocomil wind builds in the late morning and afternoon, so travel by boat in the morning.
climate.airQuality: Good in the highlands; Petén haze from agricultural burning is typical in March and April and can reduce visibility at Tikal.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Howler and spider monkeys, coatis and toucans at Tikal year-round; dry season makes birds and mammals gather at water.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Lent Sundays
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Parish procession and alfombras in Antigua each Sunday of Lent; moderate crowds.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Semana Santa
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Huge crowds and price spikes in Antigua; plan to be out before 20 March.

climate.ramadan2027: Not relevant: Guatemala is predominantly Christian; no impact on the route.
climate.tourismDemand: Dry season is high season: expect more visitors in Antigua, Atitlán and Tikal than in the rainy months; extreme only in Semana Santa.
climate.flightPriceSeasonality: Fares from Europe typically rise towards Easter and the late March holidays; a mid-February departure sits before the peak. Not verified with a live search.

geography.summary: A chain of volcanoes and highland basins from 1,500 m to over 3,900 m, a caldera lake, and the flat limestone forest of the Petén.
geography.distinctive: Fuego, one of the most continuously active volcanoes in the Americas, is watched from a campsite facing it; Santiaguito's lava dome can be seen from the Santa María summit; Lake Atitlán is the deepest lake in Central America at about 340 m.

landscapes.description: A 1,562 m caldera lake ringed by the Atitlán, Tolimán and San Pedro volcanoes.

landscapes.name: Acatenango–Fuego massif
landscapes.description: Twin peaks above Antigua; Acatenango summit 3,976 m facing Fuego.

landscapes.name: Santa María and Santiaguito
landscapes.description: A 3,772 m cone above Quetzaltenango with an active lava dome on its flank.

landscapes.name: Petén rainforest
landscapes.description: Flat, hot limestone lowlands with Tikal's canopy and Lake Petén Itzá.

culture.summary: Living Maya communities (Kaqchikel, Tz'utujil, K'iche') beside Classic Maya cities and a Spanish colonial capital.

culturalHighlights.name: Tikal
culturalHighlights.description: UNESCO-listed Classic Maya city with temples rising above the canopy; a day plus a guided sunrise.

culturalHighlights.name: Antigua Guatemala
culturalHighlights.description: UNESCO colonial city of earthquake-ruined churches and Sunday Lent processions with sawdust carpets.

culturalHighlights.name: Chichicastenango market and Santo Tomás
culturalHighlights.description: K'iche' Maya market on Thursday and Sunday, with copal burning on the church steps and at the Pascual Abaj hill shrine. Observe quietly; do not photograph rituals without permission.

culturalHighlights.name: San Juan La Laguna cooperatives
culturalHighlights.description: Women's weaving and natural-dye cooperatives in a Tz'utujil village; buying directly supports the makers.

culturalHighlights.name: Yaxhá
culturalHighlights.description: Lake-side Maya city with far fewer visitors than Tikal.

adventureHighlights.name: Acatenango overnight facing Fuego
adventureHighlights.description: 4–6 h hike to a 3,500 m camp, sub-zero night and optional 3,976 m summit; licensed operators only and only if the ascent ban is lifted.

adventureHighlights.name: Santa María dawn hike
adventureHighlights.description: Steep pre-dawn climb to 3,772 m with a guide, overlooking Santiaguito's explosions.

adventureHighlights.name: Atitlán kayaking and San Pedro volcano
adventureHighlights.description: Morning kayak on the lake; optional guided San Pedro ascent.

adventureHighlights.name: Sleeping inside Tikal
adventureHighlights.description: Camping at the park campground and a guided pre-dawn walk to the temples.

signatureExperiences.title: A night facing Fuego from Acatenango
signatureExperiences.description: Hike to a base camp at about 3,500 m and watch Fuego's explosions and lava glow through the night; optional summit sunrise at 3,976 m.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Fuego explodes 5–10 times an hour in normal behaviour and can be watched at about 2 km from a camp.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book a licensed Antigua operator only after INGUAT and CONRED confirm the ascent is open; fallback is Iximché and a day on Antigua's culture. Warm gear, sleeping bags and jackets are often hired.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Estimate for an operator package; no price verified.

signatureExperiences.title: Tz'utujil weaving villages on Lake Atitlán
signatureExperiences.description: Stay in San Juan La Laguna, visit women's dyeing cooperatives, kayak at dawn and cross to Santiago Atitlán.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Community-run cooperatives with natural dyes, on a caldera lake with three volcanoes.
signatureExperiences.location: San Juan La Laguna and Santiago Atitlán
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Walk into cooperatives in San Juan, tour with a local guide, use public lanchas in the morning, and ask before photographing.

signatureExperiences.title: Thursday at Chichicastenango
signatureExperiences.description: K'iche' market, Santo Tomás church steps and Pascual Abaj shrine.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Maya ceremonies in public places in one of the largest highland markets.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Arrive by private van on a Thursday or Sunday; go early, then continue to Xela.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Small purchases and a local guide share; estimate.

signatureExperiences.title: Santa María dawn and the Santiaguito dome
signatureExperiences.description: Climb Santa María in the dark to see Santiaguito's explosions at sunrise, then soak at Zunil's thermal pools.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: One of the few Guatemalan peaks that stay open and show a live dome from above.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Local Xela guide with a pre-arranged taxi; check INSIVUMEH status the day before.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Guide share, taxi and hot springs; estimate.

signatureExperiences.title: Sleeping at Tikal and sunrise from Temple IV
signatureExperiences.description: Camp or lodge at the park, then enter before dawn with a guide to hear howler monkeys wake the forest.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: A night inside a World Heritage jungle city rather than the day-trip crowd.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Fly GUA–Flores, use a licensed private transfer and buy tickets online; sunrise requires a guide and Q100 extra.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Entry Q150 + sunrise Q100 + guide share + camping; approximate.

travelStyle.summary: Private vans, public lanchas and one domestic flight each way, with guided volcano hikes and a night camping at Tikal; no self-drive.

transport.summary: Mostly private vans with the same driver for a stage, shared lanchas on Atitlán and a TAG or Avianca flight to Flores. Chicken buses are avoided on safety grounds; the Petén overland route is long and exposed.

modes.description: Antigua–Panajachel, Chichicastenango–Xela, Xela–Guatemala City and Petén transfers; about 3–4.5 h stages.
Minibuses between Antigua, Panajachel and Xela; cheaper but fixed schedules.
Boats link Panajachel and the lake villages; morning is calmer than afternoon.
Guatemala City–Flores, about 1 h, by TAG or Avianca; the only scheduled domestic route (Wikivoyage).
Cheap but crowded and attacked by gangs in the past; FCDO advises avoiding public buses. Not used.

transport.carRental: Rentals exist in Guatemala City and Antigua but are not used: carjacking and armed attacks on tourist routes are reported (FCDO), rental contracts can require an IDP and a minimum age, and driving in the dark is discouraged. Rental terms not verified.

drivingRequirements.summary: Legally possible for visitors holding a valid foreign licence, but not recommended on this route.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: Conditional on licence country. FCDO says a UK photocard licence is valid for up to 3 months and that hire firms can require an IDP or extra experience; other nationalities must check the local rule (commonly cited as about 30 days, not verified).
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four hold car licences. Two do not and cannot drive. Hired drivers avoid fatigue and night driving.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: Nobody may ride a motorcycle or scooter without the correct licence. Use tuk-tuks with drivers (Antigua, Atitlán), boats, private vans or guided tours.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Private vans with drivers by day; avoid public buses; book transfers in advance and do not travel at night.

accommodation.summary: Guesthouses and small hotels in Antigua, a lakeside guesthouse in San Juan La Laguna, a Xela guesthouse, a Flores island guesthouse, and the Acatenango camp and Tikal campground.

camping.summary: Camping is organised: an operator camp on Acatenango (if open) and the Tikal park campground with hired tents; wild camping is not recommended given crime and permits.

physicalDifficulty.label: strenuous
physicalDifficulty.summary: Acatenango (about 1,100 m gain to 3,500 m, to 3,976 m summit), Santa María (about 1,500 m gain), cold nights and a hot, humid Tikal day with long walking.

itinerary.summary: 13 days: Antigua (3 nights), Acatenango camp, Lake Atitlán (2), Xela (2), Flores/Tikal (3), airport night; Acatenango is replaced by Iximché if closed.

days.title: Fly to Guatemala City, private transfer to Antigua
activities: Outbound flight Paris to Guatemala City (one-stop; same-day arrival depends on the fare, not verified)
Pre-booked transfer GUA airport to Antigua after dark only with a driver arranged in advance (INGUAT airport taxi vouchers are the fallback)
Check in, cash from an ATM inside a bank or hotel, local SIM
days.transport: Flight CDG–GUA via a European or US hub; private van to Antigua
days.practical: Do not hail street taxis in Guatemala City. If the flight lands late, sleep at an airport-area hotel with transfer and go to Antigua in daylight.

days.title: Colonial Antigua on foot
activities: Walk the grid of ruined convents: La Merced, Santa Clara, Capuchinas, the cathedral ruins
Santa Catalina Arch and Volcán de Agua at first light
Cerro de la Cruz viewpoint with a hotel-arranged escort or by taxi, not on foot alone
Mercado market lunch of pepián, tamales and atol
days.culturalHighlight: UNESCO World Heritage city since 1979; baroque earthquake-ruined churches
days.geographicalHighlight: Three volcanoes frame the town: Agua, Fuego, Acatenango
days.practical: Pack warm layers: Antigua mornings are cool at about 11 °C.

days.title: Lent Sunday procession and alfombras
activities: Sunday morning: the local parish's Lent procession and the sawdust-and-flower carpets (alfombras) on its route, as described for every Sunday in Lent (confirm the parish schedule locally)
Visit a Kaqchikel weaving village such as San Antonio Aguas Calientes by shared taxi
Gear check and briefing for the volcano overnight
days.culturalHighlight: Lent Sunday procession (Sunday 14 February 2027 is the first Sunday of Lent; schedule not verified)
days.practical: Crowds are modest compared with Holy Week (21–28 March 2027).

days.title: Acatenango overnight facing Fuego (conditional on reopening)
activities: Guided ascent from La Soledad trailhead (≈ 2,400 m) to base camp at ≈ 3,500 m, 4–6 h
Evening and night watching Fuego's explosions from a cabin or tent, about -2 to 5 °C
FALLBACK if the ascent ban is still in force: day trip to the Kaqchikel capital ruins of Iximché near Tecpán and sleep in Antigua
days.transport: Operator minibus to the trailhead; hike
days.accommodation: Base camp cabin or tent (operator package); fallback Antigua guesthouse
days.geographicalHighlight: Fuego, a volcano with 5–10 explosions an hour in normal behaviour, seen from 2 km
days.practical: As of mid-November 2026 France Diplomatie still lists the Fuego/Acatenango ascent ban 'until further notice' after the August 2026 eruption; a municipal source reported Acatenango reopening on 7 August 2026 while Fuego stayed closed. Status unresolved: re-check INGUAT, CONRED and the operator before booking. Never use unauthorised trails.

days.title: Summit sunrise, descent and the road to Lake Atitlán
activities: Pre-dawn climb to the 3,976 m summit for sunrise, if conditions and authorisation allow
Descend, shower and lunch in Antigua
Private van over the Chimaltenango highlands to Panajachel (≈ 3 h), shared lancha across the lake to San Juan La Laguna
days.travelTime: ≈ 4 h hiking + ≈ 3 h road + 30 min boat
days.accommodation: Lakeside guesthouse in San Juan La Laguna, 2 twin rooms
days.geographicalHighlight: Lake Atitlán, 1,562 m, ringed by Atitlán, Tolimán and San Pedro volcanoes
days.practical: Boats stop around late afternoon when the Xocomil wind builds; arrive before dark. Fallback day: private van straight to Panajachel after Iximché.

days.title: Tz'utujil and Kaqchikel lakeside villages
activities: Visit weaving and natural-dye cooperatives in San Juan La Laguna and the mural-lined streets
Kayak on the lake in the calm morning
Lancha to Santiago Atitlán, the largest Tz'utujil town, and its Maximón shrine with a local guide (ask before photographing anyone)
Optional hike to the San Pedro volcano only with a local guide and early start (robbery incidents on some lake trails)
days.accommodation: Lakeside guesthouse in San Juan La Laguna
days.culturalHighlight: Community-run cooperatives and Tz'utujil culture around the lake
days.practical: Carry the original passport or a certified copy in San Pedro La Laguna (FCDO notes ID checks there).

days.title: Chichicastenango market and up to Xela
activities: Morning boat to Panajachel, private van north to Chichicastenango (≈ 2 h): Thursday market, K'iche' ceremonies at Santo Tomás church steps and Pascual Abaj hill shrine
Continue ≈ 2.5 h to Quetzaltenango (Xela, 2,330 m)
Evening in a cold, student-heavy highland city
days.travelTime: ≈ 30 min boat + ≈ 5 h road with market stop
days.culturalHighlight: K'iche' market town where the Popol Vuh was transcribed; Thursday and Sunday markets
days.practical: The Chichicastenango market runs Thursday and Sunday: this itinerary lands on Thursday 18 February. Keep valuables hidden; travel by day only.

days.title: Santa María volcano and Zunil hot springs
activities: Pre-dawn guided hike up Santa María (3,772 m) for views of the Santiaguito dome erupting below, ≈ 4–5 h up
Taxi to Zunil, a K'iche' village with the Fuentes Georginas thermal pools at about 2,800 m
Evening in Xela's Parque Central and market
days.culturalHighlight: Zunil village; Maximón/San Simón traditions in the Xela region
days.geographicalHighlight: Active Santiaguito lava dome seen from the summit; hot springs in cloud forest
days.practical: Alternative if you want less altitude: Laguna Chicabal crater lake day trip. Skip Tajumulco and the San Marcos side because of the rural crime warning.

days.title: Highlands to the Petén by air
activities: Early private van or first-class coach from Xela to Guatemala City airport (≈ 4–4.5 h)
Domestic flight Guatemala City–Flores (TAG or Avianca, ≈ 1 h)
Walk Flores island on Lake Petén Itzá at sunset
days.accommodation: Guesthouse on Flores island, 2 twin rooms
days.culturalHighlight: Flores island was the last independent Maya capital, Nojpetén
days.geographicalHighlight: Lake Petén Itzá in the lowland forest
days.practical: Flying avoids the long, crime-exposed overland route; NL advice is to reach Tikal by plane or organised licensed transport. Book a flight with a late-afternoon buffer.

days.title: Tikal in a full day, camping inside the park
activities: Private transfer to Tikal (≈ 1.5 h); full-day ticket Q150 on arrival (buy online in advance)
Great Plaza, North Acropolis, Temple IV with views over the canopy, Mundo Perdido
Howler and spider monkeys, coatis and toucans; ≈ 12 km of walking in 33 °C heat
Camp at the park campground (permit about Q50 per person, tent hire about Q150) or take a lodge room
days.accommodation: Tikal park campground (2 tents) or Jungle Lodge
days.culturalHighlight: UNESCO World Heritage; 8th-century Maya city with towers over 60 m
days.geographicalHighlight: Subtropical forest and ceiba trees; hot and humid
days.practical: Carry water and cash; no ticket sales at the ruins' entrance. Sunrise entry (from 04:00) needs a guide and a separate Q100 ticket.

days.title: Sunrise at Tikal, then Yaxhá at sunset
activities: Guided sunrise visit from 04:00 (extra Q100 plus a guide)
Return to the hotel or camp for breakfast
Private driver to Yaxhá (≈ 1.5–2 h, entry Q80): Maya city on a lake with a sunset view from a pyramid
Back to Flores by dark with the same driver
days.accommodation: Guesthouse on Flores island, 2 twin rooms
days.culturalHighlight: Yaxhá: far fewer visitors than Tikal
days.geographicalHighlight: Laguna Yaxhá and the Petén forest
days.practical: The guided sunrise only works if you slept at or near Tikal. Fallback: skip Yaxhá and rest in Flores.

days.title: Flores morning and the flight south
activities: Swim and kayak off Flores island or visit the Petén Itzá lakeshore
Afternoon domestic flight to Guatemala City
Stay at an airport hotel with a shuttle; do not wander zone 13 at night
days.accommodation: Airport-area hotel in Guatemala City, 2 twin rooms
days.practical: Official advice lists armed attacks in several city zones (including 13); stay in the hotel.

days.title: Fly home
activities: Hotel shuttle to La Aurora airport
Return flight GUA–CDG via a hub
Exit declaration form and departure tax (US$30, usually in the ticket)
days.practical: Arrival in Paris is the same evening or the following morning depending on the connection.

security.summary: Official advice (FCDO, Netherlands) restricts only the Mexican border strip, three Huehuetenango towns and the Izabal–Zacapa state of emergency; the redesigned route avoids all of them. Ordinary crime is high, and the Acatenango/Fuego ascent ban is an unresolved access restriction with a built-in fallback.
security.assessedRoute: Guatemala City airport, Antigua, Acatenango (conditional), Lake Atitlán, Chichicastenango, Quetzaltenango and Zunil, the Guatemala City–Flores flight, Flores, Tikal and Yaxhá. Excluded: Izabal/Zacapa, the Mexican border strip and Huehuetenango, San Marcos, El Mirador and Laguna del Tigre.

advisories.level: Against all but essential travel to parts only: 5 km Mexican border strip (Pacific coast to Gracias a Dios) and three Huehuetenango towns; rest of country no such warning
advisories.regionsAffected: Border strip, Santa Ana Huista, San Antonio Huista, La Democracia; state of emergency in Izabal and Zacapa
advisories.routeImpact: None: the route stays away from those areas

advisories.regionsAffected: Izabal and Zacapa (state of emergency from 14 Nov 2026); Petén licensed transport; border smuggling
advisories.routeImpact: Fly to Flores and use licensed transfers; avoid Izabal and Zacapa

advisories.level: Orange: 20 km Mexican border strip (San Marcos, Huehuetenango), 20 km Honduran border strip, Guatemala City zones 6, 7, 12, 18 and Villa Nueva; rest yellow (zone text 16 Nov 2026). Alert of 10 Sep 2026: Fuego and Acatenango ascents banned until further notice
advisories.regionsAffected: Mexican and Honduran border strips; Guatemala City zones 6, 7, 12, 18; Villa Nueva; Fuego/Acatenango ascents
advisories.routeImpact: Route avoids all orange zones (the airport is in zone 13). Acatenango is contradictory: the Acatenango municipality announced the trails reopened on 7 Aug 2026, while the French alert still lists a ban; keep the Antigua fallback.

advisories.level: Level 3: Reconsider travel (crime and cartel/gang terrorism); Level 4 for San Marcos, Huehuetenango, Guatemala City zone 18 and Villa Nueva (updated 11 Mar 2026; data feed)
advisories.regionsAffected: Country-wide Level 3; Level 4 departments and city zones
advisories.routeImpact: The terrorism designation is located in areas the route avoids, and the route sites (Antigua, Atitlán, Tikal) are explicitly open to US staff; treated as an ordinary-crime warning, not a conditional trigger.

conflictRisk.note: No armed conflict; gang violence and a local state of siege in Izabal/Zacapa, away from the route.

terrorismRisk.note: FCDO sees no recent history of terrorism.

kidnappingRisk.note: FCDO warns of express kidnappings from street-hailed taxis; mitigated by pre-booked transport only.

Izabal and Zacapa state of siege (14 Nov 2026, 30 days)
Mexican border strip and three Huehuetenango towns (FCDO)
Route RN14 in Sacatepéquez closed km 83–103 (France, Aug 2026)

ordinaryRisks: High violent and armed-robbery crime; armed attacks on tourist routes, carjacking
Volcano hazard and altitude; no mountain rescue
Petty theft, ATM tampering, express kidnap
Rainy-season landslides not relevant in Feb
security.medicalAccess: Good private hospitals in Guatemala City and Antigua; limited in Petén and on volcano trails; evacuation to the capital requires insurance.
security.insuranceConsiderations: Insurers may exclude volcanic eruptions or hiking above 3,500 m without a guide; check cover for trekking to 4,000 m and medical evacuation.
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check FCDO, France Diplomatie and Netherlands advice before booking and two weeks before departure; triggers: change in Fuego alert level, any new FCDO against-all-but-essential area in Petén or Alta Verapaz, extension of the Izabal–Zacapa state of siege, new road closures.

practicalRequirements.visa: Conditional on nationality. FCDO says UK passports get up to 90 days visa-free, and Wikivoyage says the same for the US, Canada and EU states; check your own passport rules.
practicalRequirements.entry: Online immigration form before entry and exit; carry a printed confirmation; CA-4 shared 90-day stay.
practicalRequirements.passportValidity: At least 6 months from arrival and 2 blank pages (FCDO for UK passports; verify for your passport).
permits: Acatenango and Fuego ascents need authorisation and a licensed guide (restricted after Aug 2026)
Tikal tickets online; sunrise needs a guide
practicalRequirements.insurance: Comprehensive travel insurance with medical evacuation and trekking to 4,000 m.
practicalRequirements.connectivity: Prepaid SIM about Q25 (Tigo or Claro); good in towns, patchy on lake trails and in the Petén.
practicalRequirements.payments: Quetzal; US dollars accepted in tourist areas; carry cash for Tikal, Uaxactún and rural stops; use ATMs inside banks and hotels.
practicalRequirements.medical: Bring a first-aid kit, DEET, altitude and diarrhoea medication; check yellow fever and measles notices (France listed a measles alert on 13 March 2026).
equipment: Warm layers, rain jacket and gloves for 0 °C nights
Dust mask or buff for volcanic ash
